rows.05:0d28:
So it's finally my turn.
I'm Makoto Shindo, third-year.
Nice to meet you all.
The story I'm gonna tell has to do with playing cards.
Cards.
There's nobody who's never played cards, right?{p}{a}, do you like playing cards?
rows.05:0e5c:
Just fifty-three cards, and there are that many different ways to play.
You can play alone, and you can play with a big group.
They don't take up any space, and all you need is the cards.
And you get that much fun out of them.
Games have come a long way lately, but if you ask me, nothing beats cards.
Whoever came up with them was a real genius.
I seriously respect them for it.
And then there's the fifty-third card.
That one really makes it.
The one they call the joker.
That thing makes cards so much more fun.
Just throwing the joker in opens up a whole lot more ways to play.
It's a magic card, no doubt about it.
I hear in the West they think the joker's bad luck, and I kind of get why.
Sometimes the joker saves your skin, and sometimes it's the last thing you want.
In short, it's an almighty card you can use any way you like.
And people hate that kind of thing, the kind you can't pin down, by instinct.{p}
rows.05:11bc:
...What?
What do cards have to do with stories about school, you ask?
Hey, don't rush me.
I'm about to start the story.
There's a guy in my class named Kazuo Okura.
That guy really knows how to get ahead in the world.
Knows how to get ahead, or, like, he's crafty... okay, to put it plainly, he's a real stickler about money.
Me, I'm more on the easygoing side, so I don't even really count how much is in my wallet.
Even if you worry about money, you just end up spending it right away, right?
{a}, what about you?{p}Are you careful with money?
rows.05:13dc:
People like that had better watch out.
They end up needing Okura's services.{p}
rows.05:1424:
Okura, see, runs a loan-sharking business at school.
And he's making a killing off it.
It's a crime, of course.
Not something anyone should get away with.
But a lot of people use him, you know.
And loan shark or not, he doesn't just lend money and collect interest.
He runs all kinds of dirty rackets at school.
Everything from buying and selling goods to doing homework for hire to running the gambling.
As for goods, they say anything you want, whether it's a computer or a pair of skis, you can get it cheap if you ask Okura.
Though supposedly it's all shoplifted.
And the really amazing part is his gambling racket.
Can you guess what it's like?{p}
rows.05:1644:
Say a fight breaks out somewhere, right?
Then he sets odds on who'll win and gets everybody to bet.
And he pockets the take.
Does he ever lose money, you ask?
Nope, not Okura.
Seems those fights are rigged.
The two doing the fighting are in on it, and who wins in the end is scripted from the start.
So he can switch the ending to whichever one pays Okura the most.
It's a fight in name only. It's really a show.
Well, everybody enjoys watching the show, so call it an admission fee.
So he's rolling in cash.
Do the delinquents shake him down? Not really.
He makes enough to hire bodyguards with it.
When I think about what he'll be like as a grown-up, it scares me.
But I bet he'll turn into one hell of a businessman.
Anyway, on to his real business, the loan-sharking.
Whoops, his real business is supposed to be studying...
He is a student, after all, technically.
Well, let's not be so uptight about it.{p}
rows.05:19bc:
You know what a loan shark is, right?
It's a business where you lend money, tack high interest onto it, and get it paid back.
Ever heard of "ten-in-ten"?
Ten-in-ten means charging ten percent interest every ten days.
And if you can't pay that interest, it gets added onto the principal you first borrowed, and the debt keeps snowballing. That's how it works.
Okura's ruthless.
He lends money at ten-in-ten, after all.
He even gets a proper signed IOU.
And what comes next is the real kicker.
He deliberately doesn't collect the interest.
First he comes up to you all smiles and lends you money, right?
Then the borrower goes to pay him back on the agreed date.{p}
rows.05:1bc4:
And then, for some reason, Okura vanishes.
So they can't pay him back.
The days just keep slipping by, and once it's swelled to an amount they can't possibly repay, that's when he goes to collect.
With his bodyguards in tow.{p}
rows.05:1ca0:
You don't hear of anything this ruthless even in the adult world, right?
So even the delinquents at the nearby schools treat Okura with respect.
There are even rumors he's become something like a shadow boss.
You watch out for Okura too.
He's got a good nose.
Once he sniffs out someone who's broke, he pops up out of nowhere and quietly creeps up on them.
And then he makes them a sweet offer.{p}
rows.05:1e0c:
"Hey, buddy.
Short on cash?
I'll lend you some, real cheap."
...Like that.
Which brings us to the cards.{p}
rows.05:1e78:
Okura's a huge gambling fan.
I mean, he even stages those rigged fight shows himself.
Life's basically one big gamble anyway, right?
It's funny, but watching Okura, I really believe that saying.
And he's especially crazy about cards.
Say poker or blackjack and he comes running.
I heard him say it once.
"I make money so I can gamble."
That's what he said.
But he's bad at it.
Hopelessly bad, Okura is.
Maybe that's why people didn't hate him yet.
He takes those high rates on his loans, but he's terrible at gambling.
He's got no luck when it counts.
So all the money he worked to make, he coughs right back up.
And so everybody figures it's fine if he takes high interest, since they can win it right back.
The world works out pretty neat, huh?
"Money goes around and around," like they say. Truer words were never spoken.{p}
rows.05:21dc:
How about it?
{a}, do you like gambling?
rows.05:2218:
I see.
{f:Guys|That's}{f: are all like that| a little unexpected}.{p}
rows.05:2260: {f:Basically,|At a glance,}{f: nobody hates gambling| you don't seem the type for it, though}.{p}
rows.05:22e4:
Then let me ask you one more thing.
Are you any good at gambling?
rows.05:2338:
Wow, look at you.
{f:Calling yourself good like that,|Dunno where you gamble, but}{f: you're either really good| if you flat-out say you're good,}{f: or just full of yourself.| you must be pretty skilled.}
...Whoa, whoa, don't get all starry-eyed,
{a}.
After hearing about Okura just now, you weren't thinking of making him your mark, were you?
Making a mark out of Okura is ancient history.
He was cute back when he was bad at gambling.
But then one day, all of a sudden, he got good.{p}
rows.05:2518:
Like he'd turned into a different person.
From then on, Okura was totally possessed by money.
He got even harsher about collecting debts, and the sums he dealt in kept getting bigger.
And almost every day he'd round people up and play poker in a corner of the classroom.
Though the crowd around him was always the same faces.{p}
rows.05:2644:
I peeked at them playing poker just once.
Apparently, under the official rules, poker doesn't use the joker.
Though there are all kinds of poker rules, so I don't know the details myself.
The poker they were playing had the joker in it.
I was just watching idly, but when I looked closer, I noticed it was a strange deck.
You know how the backs of playing cards often have a pattern or a picture on them?
That picture was creepy.{p}
rows.05:2804:
It was a picture of a woman's face, half of it a skeleton.
Split right down the middle, and the left half was a bare skull.
And the right half was a woman with a cold-looking blue face.
It was a sick picture.
Where on earth do they sell cards like that?
I was curious, so I asked.
"Hey, Okura.
Where'd you buy those cards?"{p}
rows.05:2954: And what do you think he said?
rows.05:29b0:
"These...?
These were a souvenir from my old man.
He bought 'em in some country somewhere."
Pretty curt answer, that.
Maybe he was focused on the game, but he acted like I wasn't even there.{p}
rows.05:2a6c:
I watched the game for a while.
And then I noticed something strange.{p}
rows.05:2ad4:
The joker in that deck was a skull.
And a black snake was coiled through the holes of its eye sockets.
It was a creepy joker.
But what was even stranger was that the joker always ended up in Okura's hand.
See, in poker, the joker's an almighty card you can use as anything.
Have just one of those, and you've got a big edge in the game.{p}
rows.05:2c38:
So Okura won by a landslide.
But isn't that strange?
By any odds, there's no way the joker always lands in Okura's hand.
Not unless he's cheating.
And since Okura always won, nobody was happy about it.
A few people took him on to try and beat him, but it was no use.
He cleaned them out of every cent they had, and that was that.
So rumors started that he was cheating.
Naturally, the people who hung out with him knew about the rigged fights too, so of course they'd be suspicious.
But you've got to catch a cheater in the act.
Everyone knew the joker would always land in his hand when they played poker, but nobody could figure out the secret.{p}
rows.05:2eb0:
Besides, ever since he got that deck, Okura wouldn't use any other cards, and he wouldn't take the joker out either.
Naturally, nobody played poker with Okura anymore.{p}So what do you think Okura did?
rows.05:2fc8:
He threw himself into his real business, loan-sharking.
Can you figure out why?
To force the people who couldn't pay their interest into playing poker with him.
And the terms were something else.
If you beat Okura at poker, he'd wipe out your whole debt.
But there's always a catch to a sweet deal.
What do you think happened if you lost?
He said you had to hand over your soul when you died.
Everybody laughed.
Even if you lost, all you had to do was write down, "I'll give you my soul when I die."
And on top of that, if you wrote it, you got a nice bonus: you could repay the debt whenever you liked.
In other words, for the people borrowing, it meant they practically never had to pay the money back.
Plenty of people jumped at it.
Though the serious types wouldn't even look at it.
And naturally, I didn't give it a second look either.
I mean, think about it.
Even as a joke, how could you write "I'll give you my soul"?
What is this, a pact with the devil?{p}
rows.05:3300:
As soon as they'd borrowed all they could, they'd challenge him to poker.
I mean, losing didn't cost them anything.
All they had to do was take the money and keep him company at poker.
Everybody was pretty casual about it.{p}
rows.05:33d4:
Okura never lost.
Well, the other side wasn't taking it seriously, so it was never much of a contest to begin with.
Everybody thought it was a laugh and wrote up contracts with the devil.
Okura looked happy, sitting in front of the pile of contracts he'd collected.{p}
rows.05:34b0:
It was a few days after that.
I'd stayed late at school on some errand.
Well, don't ask me why.
I've got my own stuff going on.
That's when I saw a figure in a corner of the classroom, huddled up like it was hiding.
I wondered who it was and went closer, and it turned out to be Okura.
"Okura."
Okura seemed startled by my voice.
But I was the one who got the shock.{p}
rows.05:3628:
Because he was holding a knife.
When he turned around, he was frantically trying to hide something.
But he was too late.
I saw it.{p}What do you think I saw?
rows.05:3728:
Well, to be exact, not the cards.
It was the half-skull woman painted on the backs of the cards.
I couldn't believe my eyes.
How could something like this happen?
That woman had come right out of the cards!
It was disgusting, I tell you.
And I say woman, but it was just a head.
About the size of a ping-pong ball, and it looked kind of like a shrunken head.
And there was nothing below the neck.
Well, not nothing; under the neck it was covered in tiny tentacle-like things, all squirming and wriggling.
It walked by moving those tentacles.{p}
rows.05:39d4:
"Shindo! Don't look!"
Okura threw himself over them to hide them.
But there was no way he could hide them all.
And I was frozen stiff. I couldn't even move my eyes.
What do you think Okura was doing?{p}
rows.05:3a9c:
He'd cut the pads of his fingers with the knife and was feeding them his blood.
Tiny women's heads were sucking on all five of Okura's fingers.
It was a grotesque sight.
Half of each face was a pure-white skull, right?
And yet the other half was smiling happily, like the blood tasted that good.
Eyes narrowed, half rolled back to the whites.
"These things can't live unless they eat people.
I'm out of time.
I need the souls of fifty-three people, no matter what!"
That's what Okura was screaming.
Maybe I was caught in those women's spell, because I couldn't move a single step.{p}
rows.05:3cb0:
"Shindo! Please!
Die for me!"
The fingers of Okura's left hand had those women's heads gnawing on them, right?
And he raised the knife in his right hand at me.
That's when I came back to my senses.
It felt like the women's spell had broken.
"Stop it!"
I shoved Okura away as hard as I could.{p}
rows.05:3edc:
"Stop it!
You'll get your food, like we agreed!
As long as I've got these contracts, you'll never run short of food!
The food isn't m.........."
Okura couldn't get away anymore.
The women were swimming happily in the pool of blood gurgling up out of his belly.{p}
rows.05:4080:
"Aaaaaaaaaargh!"
I let out a scream and ran for it like a madman.{p}
rows.05:40f4:
I don't remember what happened after that.
I killed Okura.
Even now, I can still see it.
...What happened to Okura after that, you ask?
Strangely enough, the bloodbath I saw in that classroom was gone without a trace, all cleaned up as if nothing had ever happened.
Okura was listed as missing.
He wasn't at home either.
He just vanished from in front of everyone, out of nowhere.
Though I'm the only one who knows the real reason.{p}
rows.05:4284:
...But you know, lately I've been thinking.
Maybe it was all just an illusion.
At least let me believe that.
Otherwise, I'm a murderer, you know?
I don't know what those women were.
I bet that deck of cards was their home.
And normally they lie in wait, plastered flat against the backs of the cards.
Though I've got no idea where those cards or the contracts are now.
But what's going to happen to the people who signed those contracts back then?
Eating a soul... how do you even eat one?
Did Okura vanish from this world without even leaving a body because his soul got eaten?
If it really happened, and those women ran off with everyone's contracts...{p}
rows.05:4514:
No, let's not think about that.
What kind of deal Okura made with them doesn't interest me, either.
It's just, even now, whenever I play cards, I make sure to take a good look at the picture on the back.
If that picture's a creepy one...
I'll tear that deck to pieces, no question.{p}And that's the end of my story.
...So now it's the last one, huh?
Let's hear it.{p}
